title: D-ID Pricing 2026: Every Plan, Cost and Limit
summary: D-ID pricing combines monthly fees with usage charges beyond each plan's base allocation. Compare tiers to choose a plan matching your video needs.
body_markdown:
## Frequently asked questions


### Is D-ID free to use?


Yes, D-ID has a free trial, but it's built for testing, not for running a product on. Expect a small allowance of credits and limits that push you to a paid plan quickly.


Use it to make a few test videos and work out your cost per finished video, then price a paid plan from that. Check D-ID's pricing page for the current allowance before you rely on it, since trial terms change.


### Does D-ID put a watermark on paid videos?


Paying alone doesn't remove it. **Watermarks are tied to the plan** , not to the act of paying. The free trial marks its output, and paid plans are where that mark comes off.


Which paid plan removes it's a detail to confirm on the plan you're considering, because a watermarked video isn't something you can hand to a customer. Run one test export on the exact plan before you commit to a month.


### Do unused D-ID credits roll over?


Treat them as not rolling over until the plan's terms tell you otherwise. Credits on subscription plans are typically tied to the billing period, so a quiet month means you paid for video you never made. That's the cost of doing nothing with them.


If your volume swings from month to month, read the expiry terms before you pick the plan, and size it to your slow months, not your busy ones.


### Can I use D-ID videos commercially?


Don't assume the free trial covers it; commercial use depends on the plan.


Paid plans are where commercial rights are generally granted, but the exact terms, including what you may do with a cloned or custom avatar, sit in D-ID's terms of service. Read those before you put a video in front of paying customers.


Fixing a rights problem after publishing costs far more than a few minutes of reading first.


### Is D-ID API pricing separate from Studio pricing?


Yes. The API's priced and metered apart from the Studio, D-ID's browser-based video editor, so a Studio subscription doesn't cover videos you generate from code.


The API has its own tiers, and those carry their own concurrency limits, meaning how many videos can render at the same moment.


If your workflow fires off many requests at once, a lower tier will queue them. Price the API on its own page, against your own volume.


Prices on both pages were not rechecked for this section, so confirm the current figures on D-ID's site before you buy.
